what_this_is: What a glance surface (an iPhone Home Screen or Lock Screen widget, and any other small surface that reads it) can show: each feed is one way to read rows from the person's own account and how to draw them, picked by the person when they add or edit the widget. `read` is either an account path (`path`, read with GET /mcp/api<path>) or a Trillion tool (`tool` and its `arguments`, called over MCP). `rows` is the path to the list in the answer (a `*` step gathers the lists of every item there into one), a tool argument written `{"$time": {"day": n}}` is the start of the day n days from today on the device, in its own time zone, `where` keeps only rows whose field equals a value (`equals`), is none of some values (`none_of`), or has a nonempty value (`present`), one test or a list of tests that must all hold, `order` puts rows whose `field` is one of `first` ahead in that order, and `show` names the path of each part the surface draws: `title`, `detail`, `note`, `done` and `total` (a progress bar when both are numbers), `time` (a date and time the surface shows as a time of day), `flag` (true marks the row) and `open` (the address a tap opens, either a path to the row's own address or `fill`, an address with {field} taken from the row; an address on one of `own_origins` opens that place in Trillion, any other whole address in the browser or app it names). `empty` is what it says when no row is left. `surfaces` names, for a surface that shows several feeds at once (the Apple Watch app, ios/Watch), which feeds it shows and in what order; its complications offer the same feeds. Read by GET /tell/feeds (src/tell-the-person.mjs) and drawn by ios/LiveActivity/TrillionGlance.swift. `surfaces` lists, per surface, the feeds it shows in order: `widgets` is the order unconfigured widgets take their feeds in, so no two show the same, and the order a large widget fills its room in after its own feed; `watch` is the watch's. A new feed is a row here and nothing else: no app update.
